title: Short Stuff: Your Dirty Bed
summary: Short Stuff episode on how dirty human beds are microbially, based on NC State University research. Josh and Chuck note that human beds contain bacteria from our own bodies (oral, skin, fecal). They contrast this with chimpanzee nests: chimps build fresh nests every night, and a study of 41 chimpanzee nests in Tanzania (15 vacuumed) found mostly environmental bacteria and no fecal bacteria typical of chimp feces, making chimps cleaner in bed than humans. The hosts discuss sleeping naked, a friend's house-fire story, and the Zippy the Chimp lovey tangent. The study is credited as "The Ecology of Sleeping" from NC State.

segments.title: Opening banter and the bed-cleanliness premise
segments.summary: Hosts banter briefly, then introduce the question of how gross human beds are, noting most people change sheets about once a week.

segments.title: Human bed microbes
segments.summary: Hosts explain that people shed trillions of microbes nightly, including oral, skin, and fecal bacteria, which end up in bed. They frame the NC State research comparing human beds with primate beds.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Hosts tease a break before returning to the chimpanzee discussion.

segments.title: Chimpanzees build new nests nightly
segments.summary: Chimpanzees construct a fresh nest every day, which the hosts find surprising. The researchers wanted to know how much of a chimp nest is the animal's own microbiome versus environmental material.

segments.title: Zippy the Chimp tangent
segments.summary: After the break, the hosts digress into childhood lovey stuffed animals, including Zippy the Chimp and a Corduroy the Bear lovey that Chuck's mom made overalls for, and a blog gallery of knockoff lovies.

segments.title: Tanzania study findings: chimp nests are cleaner
segments.summary: Researchers swabbed 41 chimpanzee nests in Tanzania and vacuumed 15. They found mostly environmental bacteria, with no oral, skin, or fecal bacteria from chimps, so chimps are cleaner in bed than humans.

segments.title: Sleeping naked and why humans bring in less outside dirt
segments.summary: Hosts discuss that sleeping naked leaves fecal bacteria on sheets, that chimps sleep naked, and that people change into sleepwear and avoid shoes in bed. A friend's house-fire story and Chuck's habit of sleeping on top of the covers come up.

segments.title: Wrap-up and credits
segments.summary: Hosts explain that chimp nests are rebuilt from scratch nightly, credit the NC State paper, and sign off with the show's production credit.
